f.title: Apply the information-grade criteria (Grade 0 to 3) to notifications
f.statement: Grade 0: identifiable patient/consumer; at least one SRAM, RAM, AE, ESAVI or other safety problem; suspect medicine or vaccine; reporter data. Grade 1 adds: onset dates of the reaction, treatment start date and treatment end date (day, month, year). Grade 2 adds: generic name; brand name; dosage; route; reason for prescription; outcome; important clinical history; batch number; manufacturer name. Grade 3 adds the result of re-administration.

f.title: Classify cases as serious using the six seriousness criteria
f.statement: Serious: any clinical manifestation with any dose of a medicine including vaccines that causes death; endangers life at the moment it occurs; requires or prolongs hospitalisation; causes permanent or significant disability or incapacity; causes alterations or malformations in the newborn; or is considered medically important. Non-serious: those not meeting these criteria.

rows.quote: 8.1.5.1 Graves (serias). A las SRAM, RAM, EA o ESAVI o algún otro problema de seguridad relacionado con el uso de medicamentos y vacunas que no cumplan los criterios de gravedad especificados en el punto 8.1.5.1, de la presente Norma.

f.title: Classify adverse reactions using the WHO-UMC causality categories
f.statement: Adverse reactions are classified according to the WHO and Uppsala Monitoring Centre causality assessment (point 10.21) into probabilistic categories. The first category, certain, covers a clinical event, including laboratory abnormalities, with a plausible time sequence to administration of the medicine, not explained by concurrent disease or other drugs or substances, with a clinically plausible response to withdrawal and pharmacologically or phenomenologically definitive, using conclusive rechallenge if necessary.

rows.actor: All members performing causality assessment (CNFV, CEFV, CICFV, UFV including MAHs)
rows.quote: 8.1.7. Las reacciones adversas se clasifican: 8.1.7.1 En concordancia a la valoración de la causalidad provista por la Organización Mundial de la Salud y el Centro de Monitoreo de la Uppsala especificada en el punto 10.21, de esta Norma, las categorías probabilísticas son las siguientes: 8.1.7.1.1 Cierta. Un acontecimiento clínico, incluyendo alteraciones en las pruebas de laboratorio, que se manifiesta con una secuencia temporal plausible en relación con la administración del medicamento, y que no puede ser explicado por la enfermedad concurrente, ni por otros fármacos o sustancias. La respuesta a la supresión del fármaco (retirada) debe ser plausible clínicamente. El acontecimiento debe ser definitivo desde un punto de vista farmacológico o fenomenológico, utilizando, si es necesario, un procedimiento de re-exposición concluyente.

f.title: Definition: medically important event or reaction
f.statement: A medically important event or reaction is a clinical manifestation or adverse occurrence that, in the physician's judgement, may not be immediately life-threatening or result in death or hospitalisation, but could endanger the patient or require medical intervention to prevent one of the criteria in the definition of a serious adverse reaction.
